title: The problem: Four active video resolutions causing half-size 4K renders
text: Fellows build videos with this toolkit and send them to a shared drive folder. Right now, whether a video came out at 4K is discovered by uploading it and looking at it. This is about five ways to find that out earlier. The capability is there. The toolkit has grown quickly and the guidance has not caught up

title: Three points of intervention: Prevent, catch locally, and detect in drive
text: Everywhere. Four different resolutions are in circulation. Someone can follow one exactly and still produce a half-size file. The five packages sit at three points. Prevent inside the toolkit so the wrong file cannot be made. Catch on the fellows' own machine before upload. Detect in the drive after it

title: Packages 1& 2: Starter blocks, CLI checklists, and toolkit size enforcement
text: Arrives. The further upstream, the fewer people involved when a problem surfaces. One, a starter kit. A block of fellow pastes before they begin, naming the two resolutions, the file name pattern, and the channel. Then one command on the finished folder that prints a green and red checklist. No permissions needed. It will not work on anyone who does not use

title: Package 3: Read-only scheduled spreadsheet reports on submission folders
text: It. Two, standardize the resolution inside the toolkit. Every instruction states the same two numbers and the toolkit declines to save a final that is not one of them. It already declines a video carrying placeholder cards, so this is a sibling of an existing rule. It needs sign-off and does nothing for what is already submitted. Three, a read-only report. A scheduled job reads

title: Packages 4 & 5: Real vs. stretched 4K frame edge checks and auto-sorting folders
text: The submissions folder and writes a spreadsheet. One row per file, grouped by fellow, with the resolution and the reason. It also lists who has not submitted. Bad videos are still made and they still arrive. Four, a real versus stretch check. It samples frames and measures how crisp the edges are, separating a genuine 4K render from a smaller one stretched to fill the frame. 48 built-in templates are defined at 1280 by 720. It gives a confidence signal, not proof. Five, sorting. The same checks, but the folder organizes itself. And whoever submitted a failing file is told the setting to change. It needs permission to move files and adds nothing the report did not already have. One thing about the size of this, packages one, three, and four are not three builds. They read the same folder and answer the same questions. Written once, the proposal is two pieces of work in a document. Your turn. If you review submissions, the question worth sitting with is which of these five would have caught the last thing you sent back? And whether that check belongs upstream of you rather than with you.
